summary: Adams County, OH tower in Shawnee State Forest; a 1934 item names towerman John Kennedy; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

ohio_fire_tower_use_ended.note: Waverly marker timeline: discontinuation of fire tower use, attributed to land-use change and improved air detection; the marker does not say when this tower stopped

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the register; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: October 27, 1934 item, transcribed from the Chillicothe Gazette, names John Kennedy as towerman and John E. Price as substitute; tower described as 60 feet high
Added to the FFLOS register September 3, 2014; nominated by Mark

evidence.supports: 60 feet high; towerman John Kennedy; substitute John E. Price
evidence.quote: The Twin Creek Tower, 60 feet high at the head of lower Twin Creek, Adams County, John Kennedy, towerman; John E. Price substitute.
Marker is in Waverly, Ohio, in Ross County.
Changes in land use and advances in air detection of forest fires resulted in the discontinuation of fire tower use.

evidence.supports: Green Ridge Tower in Pike State Forest was the last tower manned
evidence.quote: Green Ridge Tower in Pike State Forest was the last tower to be manned.

notes_for_editor: Staffing and the 60-foot height rest on an October 27, 1934 Chillicothe Gazette item as transcribed on the Eastern U.S. Lookouts page; the newspaper itself was not checked. The register gives no build date, present height or current condition, and no access level, so access is left unset. The 1978 statewide end of tower use comes from a Waverly marker and does not say when this tower stopped being used. The brief's name, agency, coordinates and elevation match the register.
